currentContext.business: The Company designs, manufactures, commissions and markets power transformers and undertakes EPC projects for electrical substations (delivery, rectification, commissioning and servicing of transformers, plus maintenance products) under its Power Systems segment. Its Industrial Systems segment develops, manufactures and markets standard and customised electric motors, magnet technology machines (including synchronous AC servo motors), and engineering/supply of drives and automation solutions. It operates exclusively in the Business-to-Business segment, serving industrial enterprises, original equipment manufacturers and government organisations.

currentContext.strengths: Capability to deliver complex, high-voltage transformer/substation projects with precision, speed and reliability|Strong, established base with public electricity utilities complemented by a diversifying customer base across national geographies|Technology capability demonstrated by successful in-house design, manufacture, testing and commissioning of 400kV class transformers|In-house manufacture and expanding product basket of Magnet Technology Machines / Synchronous AC Servo motors
currentContext.strategies: Strengthen market share across the full range of transformer voltage classes following successful entry into 400kV class manufacturing, and grow the newly-won ester oil transformer line|Projects business to pursue larger-sized projects as the next phase of growth and to specifically target booking of 400kV projects, a market not yet addressed|Grow e-mobility orders and use PLI scheme benefits plus component localization to pass on cost benefits to customers; expand into new verticals of metals, printing and packaging beyond the predominant plastics segment in Drives & Automation|Localize manufacture of drives components to mitigate currency/margin pressure|Improve market reach in the domestic gearless machines market for Magnet Technology Machines, with supply chain optimization and inventory management initiatives|Continue diversifying and widening the transformer customer base across national geographies to complement the strong existing base in public electricity utilities|Industrial Systems (motors) focus on widening market reach, refining the supply chain, and developing energy-efficient, economical products|Continuously invest in enlarging technologically advanced, superior and sustainable product offerings and augmenting facilities to capitalise on emerging opportunities|Projects business strategy of selecting quality projects and pursuing execution excellence, leveraging capability to deliver complex, high-voltage projects with precision, speed and reliability|The Company maintains a formal Dividend Distribution Policy (as required under SEBI Listing Regulation 43A for top-1000 listed entities by market capitalisation), under which the Board weighs various factors in recommending the annual dividend. Capacity expansion (Airoli transformer capacity) is being funded entirely out of internal accruals rather than fresh debt. The Company has not accepted or renewed any fixed deposits from the public. Credit rating for bank facilities has been maintained at ICRA AA- (Stable, Long Term) and ICRA A1+ (Short Term).
currentContext.expansion: The Company is expanding transformer manufacturing capacity at its Airoli works (Navi Mumbai). The original plan, intimated in the prior Annual Report, was to raise capacity from 18,000 MVA to 28,000 MVA at an outlay of about ₹170 crore; considering conducive market conditions, management revised the plan upward to 35,000 MVA at a total outlay of ₹235 crore, to be funded entirely out of internal accruals. During the year the Company successfully entered manufacturing of 400kV class transformers, secured orders for that class, began execution and commissioned a few units. Separately, on the ESG/capex-mix side, the Company reported that 12.73% of its capital expenditure in FY2025-26 (down from 22.05% in FY2024-25) went toward technologies improving environmental and social impact, citing Design Optimisation in Motors as having simplified the manufacturing process and reduced environmental impact.
currentContext.mdna: India's total installed power generation capacity has surged to 525 GW (March 2026); National Electricity Plan (2023-2032) targets 458 GW peak demand by 2032, expanding transmission network from 4.98 lakh ckm to 6.48 lakh ckm and transformation capacity from 1,398 GVA to 2,345 GVA — a multi-year structural driver for the transformer industry|Large renewable-energy capacity addition, industrial expansion, public infrastructure projects (metro lines, railway electrification, EV charging stations, data centers) and overall grid strengthening continue to drive growth for the transformer industry|Indian electric motors market projected to maintain a decent growth rate; risks.risk: Geopolitical conflict and oil-price shock (West Asia)
risks.note: The surge in global crude oil prices since the West Asia conflict, exacerbated by supply disruptions, has tilted risks to inflation on the upside and growth on the downside, with financial-channel effects (safe-haven flows, higher borrowing costs) that could hinder private investment and overall economic growth.

risks.risk: Raw material supply constraints and cost inflation for transformers
risks.note: Global demand for power transformers continues to be strong, driving demand for requisite raw materials exponentially; certain critical inputs may face supply constraints or become costlier, pressuring input costs.
Since most domestic manufacturers are expanding transformer capacity, such expanded capacity, in the absence of sustained demand, may exacerbate price competition in the industry.

risks.risk: Currency depreciation and import cost pressure
risks.note: Further widening of the current account deficit and capital outflows may lead to currency depreciation, adding to inflationary pressures through higher import prices.

Geopolitical tensions, volatility in global financial markets, and uncertainty surrounding global trade policies could pose headwinds to growth and inflation, compounded by weather-related disruptions.

The electrical motors business faces severe headwinds of intense competition that kept prices depressed despite volume growth, adversely affecting segmental margins; the Magnet Technology Machines business similarly faces severe price competition from imported brands, hurting profitability.

The Debt Equity Ratio increased sharply (to 0.15 from 0.04, up 275%) due to higher working capital borrowings and lower operating profits, while the Interest Coverage Ratio declined (to 10.28 from 14.36) on higher borrowing cost, increasing sensitivity to credit conditions.

themes.title: Transformer & grid-component shortage
themes.need: Transformer makers are running flat-out at record order books even as core-capacity ramps land (ATLANTAELE 16k->63k MVA, Q1FY27 record order book INR3,117cr on record INR972cr quarterly inflow, Vadod now PGCIL 400kV-approved with a 765kV tech tie-up in final talks; TARIL toward 75k+ MVA, Q1FY27 UEOB INR6,630cr +26% YoY on a >INR1,000cr single-shot PGCIL Ultra-Mega order, though a Changodar-expansion air-pocket held Q1 revenue to +10%; SHILCTECH adding 220kV) yet the binding constraint is still everything INSIDE a transformer - CRGO core steel, CTC/winding wire (KSHINTL/BHAGYANGR), bushings/insulators (YASHHV; 18-24mo lead, ~95% RIP/OIP imported) and transformer oil (APARINDS); both OEMs are now backward-integrating to own the bottleneck (TARIL's INR900-1,000cr CRGO/CTC/bushing/pressboard programme). Capacity-gated supply is the repeated 'need of the hour' and is driving pricing power now, though both OEMs flagged ~60,000 MVA of new 400kV capacity landing industry-wide in 3-4 months as a 1-year-out overcapacity watch-item (neither sees pricing pressure yet).
themes.driver: PGCIL Ultra-Mega order conversion (TARIL's first >INR1,000cr single-shot award) + Vadod/Changodar capacity ramps; 400kV short-circuit tests and 765kV PGCIL approvals due by Q2FY27-end are the next re-rating triggers; TARIL's Changodar restart (Aug-2026) is the swing quarter for its own growth reacceleration.
